parsed.attack: The wedge dates its own funeral: 'the eight weeks before a booked exam date.' A licensing exam is sat once in a career, the claimed moat - switching cost of history - is a card-by-card answer log that is worthless the morning after the exam, and their own floor already concedes that three-quarters of buyers may stop inside thirty days of a sixty-day cram. There is no second purchase from the same apprentice, and the content itself expires: a new code cycle every three years, per jurisdiction, means rebuilding the library for cohorts that never come back.
parsed.strongest_defence: Deadline-driven review is the one shape in this category that actually holds people - a booked exam, a licence and a pay rise supply the acuteness the cited habit apps [63][65] never had, which is exactly why Education retains where Photo and Video does not. Crucially the $29 is one-time and captured at the start, so there is no renewal to lose and no LTV exposed to month-two churn; acquisition rides on instructors and journeymen naming it to each new intake, so the replenishing cohort is the business, and the same apprentice returns years later for journeyman and master tickets.
parsed.verdict_reason: Revenue is fully captured upfront at a moment when an external deadline enforces daily use, so the first-renewal battle this surface is built on does not exist here.
